title: Where, How, and When: Query-Guided Grounding for Video Understanding

problem.summary: Understanding video content requires reasoning across multiple levels of granularity, from identifying individual objects to interpreting their relationships and localizing specific temporal actions or moments.
statements: Understanding video content requires reasoning across multiple levels of granularity, from identifying individual objects to interpreting their relationships and localizing specific temporal actions or moments.

This thesis explores three distinct grounding tasks that correspond to fundamental questions in query-guided video understanding: Where key objects are present (object-level grounding), How these objects interact (relationship-level grounding), and When specific actions occur (moment-level grounding).
These tasks collectively enable a structured interpretation of dynamic scenes in videos, progressing from fine-grained object localization to coarse temporal localization.

deploymentClaims: Traditional supervised approaches demand large-scale training datasets that cover all object types [3], relationships [4], actions, and moments [5] that may arise during deployment or test time making them difficult to scale in real-world settings.
This mismatch between training and deployment distributions creates a critical need for open-set generalization, where models must recognize and reason about novel concepts at test time.
